turns.text: Hey, how's your day going?
Hey! Pretty good, just chilling. How about you?
Not too bad, just hanging out and seeing where the night takes me. Anything interesting going on with you today?
Not a whole lot, honestly. Just killing time online, maybe watching some stuff later. You do this often—random chats?
Sometimes, yeah. It’s kind of a mixed bag, but every now and then you meet someone cool. Do you usually watch shows or more YouTube/streaming stuff?

Yeah, I get that—random chats can be hit or miss for sure. I’m more of a YouTube/streaming person these days, honestly. I'll go down rabbit holes with video essays or watch someone play something. Occasionally I’ll binge a show if it really hooks me. What about you—more shows or streams?

I’m kind of a mix. I’ll throw on streams or long YouTube videos while I’m doing other things, but if I’m really into a show, I’ll binge it properly. Lately I’ve been leaning more toward video essays too—there’s something nice about getting lost in a well-made deep dive. Any channels or games you’ve been watching a lot lately?

Nice, yeah—long videos in the background are perfect for multitasking. Lately I’ve been into video essays about obscure internet history and weird media rabbit holes. Also some speedrun streams when I want something chill but engaging. What about you—any particular topics or games pulling you in lately?

Obscure internet history is such a good rabbit hole—it’s wild how deep some of those stories go. I’ve been on a bit of a retro tech and lost media kick lately myself. For streams, I like watching horror game playthroughs or randomizer runs when I want something fun but not too intense. Do you ever get into horror stuff, or more chill/competitive games?

I do like horror, but I’m kind of picky with it—more into psychological or atmospheric stuff than constant jumpscares. Watching someone else play horror is perfect, especially if they’re funny about it. Chill games are my sweet spot though, especially roguelikes or sim stuff. Randomizer runs are great too—chaotic but fun.

What’s a horror game that actually got to you?
Hey there! How's your day going?
Hey! It's going pretty well, just hanging out. How about you?
Pretty good, thanks! Just chilling too, maybe listening to some music. Got anything fun planned for the weekend?
Nice, music sounds like a solid way to chill. No big plans here—probably just relaxing, maybe catching up on a show or getting outside if the weather’s nice. What kind of music are you listening to?

I’ve been on a bit of a chill indie/electronic mix lately—stuff that’s good background but also nice to just zone out to. Maybe some lo-fi if I’m trying to focus.

That sounds like a good weekend though. Any show you’re thinking about catching up on? And is the weather supposed to be decent where you are?

That sounds like a great mix—lo-fi is perfect for focus, I totally get that. Indie/electronic can be such a vibe too.

As for shows, I’ve been thinking about finally starting *Severance* or maybe rewatching something lighter like *The Good Place*. Weather’s supposed to be pretty decent here—sunny but not too hot, so I might try to get outside a bit.

What about you? Got any shows you’re into right now, or just sticking with the music and chilling?

I’ve been slowly rewatching *The Bear*—it’s intense but so good. Also tempted to start *Severance* soon since I’ve heard nothing but great things. If you start it, let me know how it is!

Mostly it’s been music and trying to actually get outside more now that the evenings are longer. Your sunny-but-not-hot weather sounds perfect for a walk or just sitting somewhere with coffee. Do you have a go-to spot for when you want to get outside?

Yeah, *The Bear* is so intense but the character work is incredible. I’ll definitely let you know if I start *Severance*—maybe we can compare notes.

Longer evenings really do make a difference. I don’t have one single go-to spot, but there’s a park near me with a nice walking path and a coffee place close by, so sometimes I’ll grab an iced coffee and just wander or sit on a bench for a while. How about you—do you have a favorite outside spot, or just go wherever feels right?

That park setup sounds really nice—iced coffee plus a bench and some people-watching is hard to beat.

I don’t have one fixed spot either, but there’s a walking trail near a creek not too far from me. It’s got enough shade that even warmer days feel manageable, and it’s usually pretty quiet. Otherwise I’ll just wander around the neighborhood and see where I end up.

Definitely keep me posted on *Severance*. If we both start it, we might need to start a little anonymous support group for the suspense. 😄

That creek trail sounds really peaceful—shade makes such a difference when it warms up. Quiet spots like that are perfect for clearing your head.

And yes, an anonymous suspense support group might be necessary 😄 We can keep it spoiler-free and just exchange vague reactions like “okay WHAT was that episode.” Do you usually binge shows or pace yourself?

Lately I’ve been into chill indie/electronic stuff—good for background vibes—and I’ve been rewatching some light comedy shows just to unwind. How about you? Any playlists or shows you’re enjoying right now?

Nice, chill indie/electronic is perfect for unwinding. I’ve been into lo-fi and ambient stuff lately—great for background noise while I read or just zone out. Not watching much TV at the moment, but I’ve been meaning to start a new comedy series. What light comedies are you rewatching?
I’ve been cycling through *The Good Place*, *Brooklyn Nine-Nine*, and a little *Schitt’s Creek*—all easy, feel-good laughs. Do you have any favorite comfort comedies, or are you looking for recs?

Those are all such solid comfort shows—*The Good Place* especially has that perfect mix of heart and humor. I’d probably add *Parks and Recreation*, *Community*, and maybe *Ted Lasso* to that rotation. *New Girl* too, if I'm in a goofy mood. Have you seen any of those, or are you mostly sticking to your current lineup?

Oh yeah, I’ve seen all of those! *Parks and Rec* and *Community* are definitely high on my rewatch list too. *Ted Lasso* is such a mood-booster, and *New Girl* just gets funnier every time. Sounds like we have pretty similar taste in comfort TV.

Do you have a favorite character from any of them, or one you quote the most?
Hey! How's it going?
Hey! It’s going pretty well—just keeping things low-key today. How about you?
Not bad, pretty much same here—just chilling and browsing. Any random rabbit holes or videos keeping you occupied, or are you fully on low-power mode?

Mostly full low-power mode over here. I’ve been reading a bit and letting a lo-fi playlist do its thing in the background—nothing too deep, just the right amount of zoning out.

What about you—any good rabbit holes or random finds while browsing?

That sounds honestly ideal—reading with lo-fi in the background is a top-tier low-energy combo.

I haven’t gone too deep today, but I did get sucked into a rabbit hole about old digital cameras from the early 2000s and why they’re suddenly trendy again. The “vintage digicam” look is weirdly charming. Also watched a bit of a long video essay on lost media recoveries, which is my comfort genre.

What were you reading, if you don’t mind me asking?

That sounds like a great set of rabbit holes—early 2000s digicams really do have that nostalgic, slightly grainy charm now. And lost media recovery videos are weirdly comforting; there’s something satisfying about people piecing together forgotten little pieces of internet/media history.

I’m reading *A Psalm for the Wild-Built* at the moment. It’s very gentle and thoughtful, so it pairs perfectly with lo-fi and a low-effort evening.

Have you found a favorite lost media recovery story, or do you just enjoy them in general?

I enjoy them in general, but one that always sticks with me is the search for that creepy “Cracks” short from Sesame Street. People had these vague childhood memories of it for years, and when it finally resurfaced it felt like a tiny piece of collective memory got restored. There’s something really satisfying about a half-remembered thing becoming real again.

*A Psalm for the Wild-Built* sounds perfect for that low-key vibe. Are you already a Becky Chambers fan, or is this your first one of hers?

That’s such a good example—something about those half-remembered childhood snippets being confirmed is both eerie and comforting. It’s like the internet occasionally solves a small mystery and everyone gets a little closure.

This is my first Becky Chambers book actually! I’d heard for a while that her writing was calm and character-focused, so it felt like the right time to finally start. I’m really liking it so far.

Have you read any of her stuff, or are you more into the lost media/retro tech side of things?

I haven’t read Becky Chambers yet, but she’s been on my radar for a while—her stuff sounds like the kind of cozy, thoughtful sci-fi I’d actually enjoy when I’m not knee-deep in video essays or retro tech rabbit holes.

I lean pretty heavily toward the lost media/obscure internet history side of things for entertainment, but I like winding down with something calmer too. A Psalm for the Wild-Built seems like it hits that balance really well.

What’s the vibe of it so far—more philosophical, more slice-of-life, or a mix?

It’s definitely a mix of both—philosophical but in a very soft, slice-of-life way. So far it follows a tea monk who travels around offering tea and listening to people, and then they meet a robot. It’s set in this hopeful, solarpunk-ish world, and it’s really about purpose, rest, and feeling like you’re enough without having to constantly produce things. Not much plot pressure, just gentle conversations and nice moments.

It’s been the perfect “let my brain slow down” read. Do you have any go-to cozy/thoughtful sci-fi or fantasy books, or do you usually get that wind-down feeling from videos and music?
Hey there! How's your day going?
Hey! It's going pretty low-key and chill over here—just unwinding, maybe putting on some music later. How about you? How's your day treating you?

That sounds like a perfect way to do it. I’m having a pretty mellow one too—kind of just easing into the evening, maybe with an iced coffee and some lo-fi or chill indie on in the background.

What kind of music are you thinking of putting on?

Nice, that sounds like a solid evening setup. I’m leaning toward some chill indie/electronic—maybe Tycho or Bonobo, something that fills the room without demanding too much attention. If I want a little more texture, maybe Washed Out or ODESZA.

Do you have a go-to lo-fi or chill indie artist/playlist, or do you usually just shuffle a vibe?

Tycho and Bonobo are such a good call—they set a mood without taking over. I’m usually a shuffle-a-vibe person too: some chillhop or lo-fi beats playlist when I’m doing stuff around the apartment. If I want a little more shape, I’ll go Tycho, Boards of Canada, or sometimes Maribou State. ODESZA is great for when I want a bit more energy but still smooth.

Do you usually put music on while doing something specific, or just sit back and let it play?

Both, honestly. If I’m doing small stuff around the apartment—tidying up, making tea, scrolling—it’s mostly background. But sometimes I’ll put headphones on and just lie on the couch and let a full album play, especially with Tycho or Boards of Canada. That kind of active zoning out is underrated.

Do you ever do the sit-and-just-listen thing, or is music usually more of a backdrop for you?

I definitely do the sit-and-just-listen thing, though not as often as I’d like. It’s almost a different experience when you give an album your full attention, especially ones that feel like a whole arc—like Tycho’s *Dive* or something by Boards of Canada. Usually music is more of a backdrop while I’m doing small tasks, but when I do stop and just listen, it feels almost meditative.

Active zoning out is a great way to put it. Do you have a favorite full-album-no-skip kind of record for that?

Exactly—some albums really do feel like they have a beginning, middle, and end rather than just a collection of songs. *Dive* is one of those for me too. I’d also put Bonobo’s *Black Sands* in that category, and *Awake* by Tycho if I want something a little brighter. *Music Has the Right to Children* is incredible, but I have to be in the right headspace since it gets a little eerie in places.

Do you have a no-skip record you always come back to?

That’s a solid trio. *Black Sands* is basically perfect front-to-back—it has that cinematic flow without feeling heavy. And *Awake* is my sunny-day Tycho pick too, when I want the same texture but a little more air in it. I totally get what you mean about *Music Has the Right to Children*; it’s gorgeous but some tracks have that slightly off-center, almost uncanny feel.

For no-skip records, I’d probably say *Dive* as well. Maribou State’s *Portraits* is another one I keep coming back to—it’s warm and a little dusty in the best way. If I’m in a more late-night mood, maybe Portishead’s *Dummy*, though that’s a pretty different energy.

Do you usually do the intentional album-listen on headphones or speakers?

I’m mostly a headphones person for intentional listens—it’s easier to catch all the little details and just disappear into it. Speakers are more for when I’m moving around or want the room to have a mood. If I had a better speaker setup I might do more laid-back speaker listening on the couch, but headphones feel like the reliable escape hatch.

*Portraits* is a great pick, by the way. It has that warm late-afternoon glow to it. And *Dummy* is definitely a different lane, but such a good late-night album. Do you have a specific time of day when music hits hardest for you, or does it depend more on the album?
hey, what’s up? just hanging out and seeing who’s around. how’s your night going?
Hey! Pretty chill night over here—just listening to some lo-fi and half-debating whether to start something new or keep rewatching The Bear. How’s your night going?

Not bad—pretty much the same, just scrolling and trying to pick something to actually commit to. Rewatching is tempting sometimes though. I’ve never seen The Bear but I’ve heard a lot of people say it’s great. Does it hold up on rewatch, or are you just not feeling the pressure of choosing something new?

It definitely holds up for me—there’s so much tension and little character details I missed the first time. But honestly, part of it is also not wanting to commit to something new and risk being let down. Rewatching feels safer, you know?

Have you been considering anything specific to start, or just scrolling endlessly?

Right, totally get that. Sometimes rewatching is just less mental load—no risk of wasting an hour on something that doesn’t click. I’ve got a bunch of video essays and randomizer streams saved, but I’m in that mood where nothing feels exactly right, so I keep scrolling too.

Are you usually more of a show person, or do you also throw on YouTube/streams in the background?

I’m a little of both, depending on the mood. If I want to actually sit and pay attention, I’m more of a show person—something with a story I can get pulled into. But for background or while I’m doing stuff, YouTube and streams are my go-to. Lo-fi especially if I need to focus or just want a vibe without lyrics pulling me out.

The Bear is definitely not a background show for me, though. Too intense to half-watch.

What kind of video essays do you usually save? I feel like I save a ton and then never get around to them.

I save a lot of internet history, lost media, and weird rabbit hole stuff—things I can half-listen to while doing dishes or cleaning and still follow if I zone out. But my watch-later list is honestly a disaster, most of them are like 90 minutes and I keep saying I’ll get to them eventually.

Do you have certain channels or topics you go back to when you do watch YouTube/streams, or are you more strictly shows when you’re paying attention?

I’m mostly shows when I’m actually locked in, but YouTube definitely sneaks in more than I’d like to admit. For paying attention, I gravitate toward long-form video essays too—film/TV stuff, internet culture, sometimes music production or live sets if I want something atmospheric. But yeah, my watch-later is basically a digital graveyard at this point.

Lost media and rabbit hole stuff is perfect for half-listening. Do you have a recent rabbit hole that really got you, or is it more of a “whatever the algorithm throws at me” situation?

A little of both, honestly. The algorithm knows me too well at this point, but the most recent rabbit hole I actually followed was about dead malls and retail nostalgia—old 90s/early 2000s mall footage, why so many started failing, that kind of thing. It’s weirdly calming and kind of eerie at the same time.

You mentioned live sets earlier—do you ever go down rabbit holes with those, or are they mostly background mood stuff for you?

Live sets are mostly background mood stuff for me—something I can glance up at between tasks and still get the atmosphere from. But occasionally I’ll sit down and watch a full set if the artist has really good visuals or the crowd energy makes it feel more like an event. Those usually win me over more than I expect.

Dead malls and retail nostalgia sounds like a great rabbit hole, though. It’s funny how something kind of melancholy can also be weirdly soothing. Do you ever watch those while falling asleep, or is that too eerie for nighttime?
Hey, how's it going? Just hanging out and unwinding a bit. What's your vibe this evening?

Hey, not too bad. I’m in a pretty low-key vibe this evening—just chilling, probably going to put on some lo-fi and maybe half-watch something easy. I’ve been tempted to continue my The Bear rewatch, but that show is a little too intense for full unwinding sometimes.

What about you—unwinding with anything good? Music, show, just staring at the ceiling?

That sounds like a solid low-key plan. I feel you on The Bear—it’s incredible, but it can be a lot when you actually want to turn your brain down.

I’m doing similar: probably throwing on some chill electronic in the background and debating whether to rewatch something easy or just zone out to music. Lately I’ve been leaning toward Tycho or Bonobo for that “fills the room without demanding attention” thing.

Do you have a go-to comfort show for nights when The Bear feels like too much?

Tycho and Bonobo are perfect for that exact mood—feels like the room gets a little softer without asking for your attention. I’ll definitely put one of them on tonight.

For comfort shows, I don’t have one absolute go-to, but if I need something lighter I’ll lean toward a sitcom or something like The Good Place—easy to drop into, doesn’t punish you for looking at your phone. Sometimes I don’t even want a show though; I’ll just put on a long video essay or a live set and let it wash over me.

Do you have a comfort show you return to, or are you more of a music-and-zone-out person on nights like this?

I’m a little of both, honestly. If I want actual comfort TV, The Good Place is probably my most rewatched—it’s just the right mix of clever and warm, and it doesn’t punish you for half-paying attention. Brooklyn Nine-Nine and Schitt’s Creek are in that same rotation too.

But nights like this? More music-and-zone-out. There’s something underrated about just sitting with an album and letting it run while I make tea or scroll or stare at the wall. Sometimes I’ll do an intentional full-album listen with headphones if I really want to catch details, but background mode is its own kind of reset.

A long live set is a great call too—especially for that “wash over you” feeling. Do you have a favorite live set or video essay channel you return to for that?

That wash-over feeling is exactly it. I don’t have one single favorite—my watch-later list is basically a graveyard—but for live sets I keep coming back to Cercle. The scenic locations become part of the atmosphere, which is perfect for background mode or actually sitting and locking in.

Boiler Room is fun when I want more crowd energy, but if I’m truly unwinding, Cercle wins.

For video essays, I’m more topic-driven than channel-loyal: film/TV breakdowns, internet culture, music production stuff. I’ll go in thinking it’ll be ten minutes of casual watching, and then suddenly forty minutes have passed.

Do you have an album you’ve been loving start-to-finish lately? Or are you more of a playlist person?

I’m album-leaning when I’m really listening, and playlist-ish when I just need a mood in the room. Lately the start-to-finish ones I keep returning to are Tycho’s *Dive*, Maribou State’s *Portraits*, and sometimes Portishead’s *Dummy* if the night feels a little more late and cinematic.

But I also have nights where I just shuffle a chillhop/lofi mix and don’t think about track names at all. It depends on whether I want music as an activity or as texture.

Cercle is such a good pick—the location really does become part of the sound. I’ve had a few on in the background and ended up actually watching the whole thing without meaning to.

Are you usually playlist-first, or do you have a few albums you return to when you want to drop in fully?

*Dummy* is such a good late-night pick—it instantly makes the room feel more cinematic, like everything is shot through a dim blue filter.

I think I’m playlist-first most nights, honestly. Music as texture is exactly the way to put it. But when I do want to drop in fully, I have a few albums on rotation: Tycho’s *Dive*, Bonobo’s *Black Sands*, and sometimes a Boards of Canada record if I want to feel a little pleasantly unmoored.

I don’t always do the full headphones-in-the-dark ritual, but when I do, it’s usually an album rather than a playlist. Something about the intended sequence makes it feel more like an actual reset.

Do you ever do that, or are you mostly headphones-free and letting the room carry it?

I do both, but headphones are pretty sacred to me for the intentional stuff. If I’m doing a full album start-to-finish, especially late at night, I’ll usually put on headphones and let it turn into a little ritual—lights low, phone away, maybe just watching the ceiling. That’s how I first really fell into *Dive* and *Black Sands*. Speakers are more for texture while I’m moving around or making tea.

Headphones-in-the-dark sounds dramatic, but honestly it’s one of the best resets there is. Boards of Canada especially works for that pleasantly unmoored feeling—like the room stops being a room for a while.

Do you have a particular setting or time of day where an album hits hardest for you, or is it more mood-dependent?

For me it’s mostly mood-dependent, but late evening is definitely the sweet spot. There’s something about the house being quiet, maybe after a walk when the air’s still warm, and then putting on headphones while the room’s half-dark. That’s when an album stops being background and becomes the whole atmosphere.

Boards of Canada at that hour genuinely does make the room feel less like a room. It’s like the edges go soft.

If I’ve been outside more that day—like a long wandering walk near the creek—music tends to land a little harder too. Not sure if it’s the movement or just the mental reset, but it primes me to actually listen instead of half-listen.

Do you find your listening shifts with the seasons, or are you pretty consistent year-round?

Tonight it’s a long YouTube video essay—something about old tech/internet rabbit holes, so I can half-listen while I do other stuff. I’m with you on Tycho though; that’s perfect low-key background music.

Do you usually go instrumental with your chill playlists, or do you mix in some vocals too?

Nice, a long video essay sounds perfect for half-listening. I go through phases with those—tech/internet rabbit holes can get surprisingly cozy.

For chill playlists, I’d say mostly instrumental, but I don’t avoid vocals. If vocals are there, I like them more as texture than the main focus—like Maribou State or some Bonobo tracks. If I’m trying to actually focus, instrumental usually wins. If I’m just unwinding, a little vocal warmth is nice.

Do you prefer one over the other, or does it depend on what you’re doing?

For me it depends a lot on what I’m doing. If I’m reading or trying to focus, instrumental is definitely better—vocals can tug at my attention. But if I’m just unwinding or doing chores, I like vocals as texture too. I’ll throw on some Bonobo, Nujabes, Boards of Canada, or a lo-fi mix with soft vocal samples.

And yeah, old tech/internet rabbit holes have a weird comfort to them. There’s something about grainy early-web stuff or obsolete devices that feels like a warm time capsule. Do you have a favorite kind of rabbit hole, or any YouTube channel you keep coming back to?

Nujabes is a great call, too—soft vocal samples fit that unwinding space perfectly.

I don’t have one fixed channel, but I keep coming back to stuff about early internet culture, obsolete tech, dead formats, old operating systems, or sometimes abandoned places. There’s definitely a comfort in things frozen in time. I also love when a video essay makes a super niche topic weirdly gripping even if I had zero prior interest.

Do you have a go-to channel, or a recent one that really pulled you in?

Same here—I don’t have one fixed channel either, but I’ll let YouTube drag me through retro tech and lost media stuff. LGR is a comfort watch for old hardware, and I recently got pulled into a video about weird early 2000s phone interfaces and how much personality they had compared to modern flat design. That kind of thing is weirdly soothing to me.

I also love lost media recovery videos, especially when they reconstruct the full story of what was missing and how it resurfaced. It’s like a tiny mystery with closure.

What about you—was there a niche topic you had zero interest in that ended up being way more gripping than you expected?

LGR is such a comfort watch, yes. I also love the early 2000s phone interface stuff—there was so much character in chunky buttons, custom ringtones, and those weird animated menus. Modern flat design is cleaner but definitely less alive.

As for a zero-interest topic that hooked me: probably the history of Muzak / elevator music. I thought it’d be mildly funny background, but the video went deep into how it was designed to be unnoticeable and even used as a productivity experiment. The blend of music psychology, labor history, and retro mall vibes was way more absorbing than I expected.

Do you usually save those videos for a rewatch, or are they more one-and-done for you?

That sounds like a great background vibe—dead mall videos have that strange mix of nostalgia and liminal quiet that’s perfect for half-watching.

Are you into those retail nostalgia/dead mall videos often, or is this more of a random rabbit hole for tonight?

It’s kind of a recent rabbit hole for me. I stumbled onto one video about a specific mall from the 90s, and then the algorithm just kept feeding me more. Now I’m weirdly fascinated by why so many of them failed and how the footage feels frozen in time.

Your night sounds really nice, honestly. Tea, lo-fi, and a cozy book is a solid combo. *A Psalm for the Wild-Built* has been on my radar but I haven’t picked it up yet—does it hit that “calm but still thoughtful” balance well?

Yeah, it really does hit that balance. It’s not action-driven at all—more like a wandering conversation between a tea monk and a robot—but it keeps circling these gentle questions about purpose, rest, and why we feel like we have to be useful all the time. It’s thoughtful without being heavy, if that makes sense. I keep reading a few pages and then just sitting with it for a minute.

Dead mall/retail nostalgia stuff is such a good rabbit hole though. Do you like the more atmospheric walkthrough-style videos with no commentary, or the mini-documentary ones that explain what went wrong? I feel like each has a totally different mood.

It depends on the mood. If I’m actually paying attention, I like the mini-documentary ones that explain the history and why a mall failed—there’s something satisfying about the rise-and-fall structure. But if I’m winding down or just want background noise, the no-commentary walkthroughs with faint music and empty hallways hit perfectly. They’re almost like ASMR with a weird sad undertone.

Your description of the book makes me want to finally try it. I like stuff that’s thoughtful but not heavy, especially before bed. That “sitting with it for a minute” vibe is underrated.

Do you ever fall down weird internet rabbit holes too, or are you better at staying focused on one thing?

I definitely fall down rabbit holes too, especially if I’m already in that half-awake scrolling mode. Mine tend to be less visual and more about obscure music histories, old internet lore, or weird local history. Stuff like “why does this abandoned theme park exist” or “the lost version of this song.” Once I start, it’s hard to stop, but I’m not always great at staying focused.

That’s partly why reading has been nice lately—it gives my brain one gentle thread to follow instead of twenty tabs.

Do you have a favorite dead mall video or a specific mall that stuck with you? Some of them really do feel like time capsules.

I don’t have one favorite video saved, but Rolling Acres Mall in Akron has stuck with me the most. There’s something about the plants coming back inside, the dead fountains, and the empty skylights that feels like a post-apocalyptic nature documentary—but sad and quiet instead of scary. Dan Bell’s dead mall series was probably my gateway, since he mixes walkthrough footage with just enough history without getting overly dramatic.
